findings.title: Readiness does not enforce the fallback requirement for non-independent CI
findings.trigger: A fork or non-owner, non-bot PR changes .github/, or its change set cannot be determined, while the supplied evidence contains an otherwise valid COMPLETE inspection-only record and no owner fallback.
findings.execution_path: runCli computes ciDefinitionsChanged; readiness labels CI as not-independent but does not pass that restriction to codexStatusFor. The latter accepts the COMPLETE inspection record. The final every() treats not-independent as sufficient and returns ready: true.
findings.consequence: A stale or inconsistent COMPLETE record can bypass the newly documented owner-fallback requirement. Failure to determine the .github/ change set also does not actually fail closed when COMPLETE evidence is supplied.
findings.evidence: Using the existing inspectionOnlyBaseline fixture with an outsider fork and ciDefinitionsChanged=true returned ready=true, fallback=null, CI ready=not-independent, and Codex=ok. All 223 existing acceptance/fallback tests passed. The test titled 'a not-independent head is ready only through the owner-approved fallback' supplies an INCOMPLETE status, so it never exercises a conflicting COMPLETE record; adjacent tests assert only the displayed CI label.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the independently computed CI-independence restriction into the Codex acceptance decision. Reject COMPLETE evidence that conflicts with this restriction and require the documented fallback path. Add regression assertions for COMPLETE evidence with changed and unknown .github/ change sets, for both forks and same-repository non-bot contributors.
